summary: Kootenai NF 45-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab, built 1936 per firelookout.com; the page and the FFLA Montana list both say it is gone.

facts.design: 45-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab
facts.status_note: firelookout.com says it has been gone for quite some time and leaves the end date open. The FFLA list says Tower Gone. No source describes what remains.

evidence.supports: built in 1936 as a 45-foot pole L-4 tower; gone for quite some time
evidence.quote: Built in 1936, this 45' pole L-4 tower has been gone for quite some time.

evidence.supports: FFLA lists the tower as gone
L-4 cab is a 14-by-14-foot frame cab a lookout could live in; these could be placed atop tall fire towers
evidence.quote: 14'x14' frame cabs were made to live in and could be placed atop tall firetowers.

notes_for_editor: Thin. One lookout page (firelookout.com) gives the build year, design and elevation; the FFLA Montana list confirms Tower and Gone. The Lincoln County page on montanalookouts.weebly.com lists Keno Mountain under Kootenai NF (36N-34W-32) with no history, so it is not cited. No removal date. Height is not recorded: the page says 45' pole, which could be pole length rather than height above ground, so height_m is left out. Elevation 6,542 ft is only in the story. No photo added; the page credits a Fire Lookout Museum photo but no image URL was found in the cache.
